paper text.text:
The graph $G$ has $K$ as a minor by retaining $B$, the edge $cd$,
and shortening $apc,brd$ to $ac,bd$. Thus $K$ has no $K_5$ minor.
By the equivalence just proved, replacing $B$ by an allowed minor $B'$
gives a nontoroidal graph whenever $B'+ac+cd+bd$ is nonplanar.
Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}, with attachments $a,b,c,d$ and
added edges $ac,cd,bd$, therefore lists all $15{,}626$ candidate forms
of $B$. Adjoining $\Psi_1$ and $af$ to each candidate gives a graph
with a $K_5$ minor or a proper nontoroidal minor~\supp{E2}, a
contradiction. Therefore $B$ does have a disk drawing in the order $a,b,d,c$, and Lemma~\ref{dis:four-root-isolation} implies $D$ is a single vertex.
\end{proof}

vertex names: a = s1, b = t1, c = s2, d = t2, e = s3, f = t3; twins p, q on {a, c, e} and r, z on {b, d, f}; the paths are the edges ab, cd, ef. Interior vertices of B are i0, i1, ...
the case: G = (Psi_1 ∪ B) + af, where B has attachments A = {a, b, c, d}. The candidates are the graphs B of Construction 3.18 with attachments A, added edges E = {ac, cd, bd} and no required edges: A independent in B, interior nonempty and connected, every attachment with an interior neighbour, and B + E nonplanar (each candidate gives a Kuratowski subgraph).
verdicts: Every candidate gets a proper nontoroidal minor obtained by deleting or contracting one edge of G (a contraction merges the second vertex into the first). The witness says why that minor is nontoroidal.
